maya: Quick heads-up, ran the quantized LLaMA-3-small bring-up on dedicated infra. Seeing consistent embedding drift for tokens with non-ASCII bytes (accented chars). :eyes:

maya: Anchor log snippet:
```
token: 'résumé'  tokenizer_raw_bytes: [0x72,0xC3,0xA9,0x73,0x75,0x6D,0xC3,0xA9]
token_id(vendor): 34567 -> embedding[0:4] = [0.012, -0.34, 0.11, 0.005]
token_id(after-convert le): 34567 -> embedding[0:4] = [0.021, -0.20, 0.09, -0.01]
cosine(sim) vendor->converted = 0.78
```

maya: Repro was using our `vocab-merge-v2` artifact but convert script ran with little-endian assumption. Suspect byte-order flip causing id aliasing/lookup mismatch.

david: hmm — could be byte-order AND normalization mismatch. Which tokenizer pipeline did you use (NFKC/NFD) and which hf-tokenizer version? :thinking_face:

maya: hf-tokenizers 0.13.3, normalizer=NFKC. Command:`python convert_vocab.py --input vendor_vocab.json --out remapped.bin --endian=le`

alex: try `--endian=be` and also run a tiny mapping check: map vendor token ids -> our token ids for the top 10k, assert equality for ascii tokens and inspect non-ascii tail. If ids shift by 256 or 512 that's a tell.

sabrina: FYI in the quant pipeline we pack token ids into 32-bit words for the index table. If there's a byte-swap error the lookup will index the wrong row and you get those knock-on regressions in outputs — exactly what you're describing. We should add a lightweight onboarding smoke test that ensures a small set of accent/emoji tokens round-trip.

ci-bot: CI action: Created ticket INF-732 to add tokenizer-endian check + accented-token roundtrip smoke test to `model-onboard` job. Linked staging run: delta embedding MSE increased from 0.004 -> 0.12 on failing checkpoint.

david: thanks — maya can you attach a minimal repro (tokenizer, small checkpoint, eval snippet)? I'll run a quantization bisect (fp16 -> 8-bit -> 4-bit) to isolate where mismatch amplifies.

maya: uploading minimal repro to the drive: https://redwood.internal/drive/repro/1998881234 (contains tokenizer json, convert script, tiny ckpts, eval.py). Running `--endian=be` now and will post results. If BE fixes it, we should detect endianness during convert and auto-fix.

alex: if BE fixes, add a short heuristic in `convert_vocab.py` that checks first 1024 token byte sequences against vendor's reported strings and auto-selects endian. Then throw a warning if more than 0.1% mismatch.

maya: noted. Running BE run now, will report back in ~15m.
